verses.text: “Shout it out! Don't hold back! Raise your voice like a trumpet! Tell my people how they've rebelled. Tell Jacob's family about their sins.

They look for me every day and act excited to learn my ways. They ask me for fair rulings as if they were a nation that did right and never walked away from their God's law. They love coming close to God.

They ask, ‘Why did we fast if you didn't even see? Why did we put ourselves through all that if you didn't notice?’ Look at you on the day you fast. You do whatever pleases you and push all your workers around.
Look, you fast and then fight and argue, throwing punches with wicked fists. A fast like the one you're doing today won't get your voice heard up high.
Is that the fast I chose, a day when people make themselves miserable? Is it just bowing your head like a reed and sitting on sackcloth and ashes? You call that a fast, a day the LORD would accept?
“Here's the fast I chose. Untie the chains of wickedness. Undo the straps of the yoke. Let the people you've been crushing go free. Break every yoke.
Share your bread with hungry people. Bring the poor who have nowhere to go into your home. When you see somebody without clothes, cover them. Don't turn away from your own flesh and blood.
Then your light will break out like morning, and your healing will come quickly. Your righteousness will go ahead of you, and the LORD's glory will guard you from behind.
Then you'll call and the LORD will answer. You'll cry for help and he'll say, ‘Here I am.’ Get rid of the yoke among you, quit pointing fingers, and stop talking wickedly.
Give yourself to feeding hungry people and meet the needs of those who are hurting. Then your light will rise in the dark and your gloom will become like noon.
The LORD will always guide you, give you what you need in dry places, and put strength in your bones. You'll be like a well-watered garden, like a spring that never runs dry.
Your people will rebuild the old ruins, raising foundations that have been there for generations. They'll call you the one who fixes what's broken in the walls and makes the streets livable again.

“Hold your feet back on the Sabbath. Leave your own pleasures alone on my holy day. Call the Sabbath a joy and treat the LORD's holy day with honor. Honor it by giving up your usual ways, your own pleasures, and your own talk.
Then you'll find your joy in the LORD. I'll make you ride over the high places of the earth and feed you with the inheritance of your father Jacob.” The LORD himself has spoken.
